steps.content: [Background - Dining Car]
After Carl leaves, you continue observing the passengers in the dining car, but nothing else of note catches your eye.

Rain begins to fall as night sets in. The clattering of silverware gradually fades, the desserts are cleared away, and the wine glasses have run dry by now. One by one, passengers rise from their seats and return to their compartments.
Lingering for too long after everyone else has left would only draw suspicion. You fold up the newspaper and stand up.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Clementine, you can head back first.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hm?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: I'm going to check the other carriages. There are a few things I still want to look into.
[Background - Corridor]
You return to the corridor. However, instead of heading to the corner where Clementine found the letter, you turn and stop in front of Carl's compartment.

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: Still... to be chosen as her companion... Hehe, I'm not sure if I should call you lucky, or unlucky.
You raise your hand.
Knock knock...
You wait for a moment. The compartment is completely silent—you hear no footsteps, nor do you see any shadows beneath the door. It seems Carl hasn't returned.
Just as you're about to leave, you hear the sound of an argument coming from the other end of the corridor.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Is someone there?
You tiptoe toward the other end of the corridor. As you draw closer, the sounds of the argument grow louder. They're coming from the neighboring compartment, Room 102.

steps.speaker: Muffled Voice
steps.content: <color=#7683a2><size=28>...What do you mean? Didn't we agree...</color></size>

steps.speaker: Muffled Voice
steps.content: <color=#7683a2><size=28>****, it's all because of...</color></size>
Who could they be? The voices come in fragments, drowned out by the grinding of wheels against rails.
You press yourself against the wall and edge closer to the corner in an attempt to hear more.

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: You better get the hell out of here! Don't screw this up!
A furious shout rings out beside you. The next second, the door is flung open. William storms out, his menacing figure filling the doorway as he comes face-to-face with you.
His piercing gaze sweeps over you, his already harsh features twisted into something demonic.

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: You... were you eavesdropping?
His shoulders tense up as he speaks. His fist is already raised. You try to explain yourself, but any movement or another word would come far too late to stop what's coming—
Just then, another voice stops William in his tracks. The elderly woman stands in the middle of the corridor, clutching a small bag, her expression uneasy.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: Young person, do you know where Room 103 is?
William glances at her, then looks back at you.
The air hangs heavy for about two seconds. Finally, he lets out a cold snort, lowers his fist, and goes back into his room.

You finally let out a sigh of relief. The elderly woman beside you seems completely oblivious to the tense situation just moments before, perhaps due to her poor eyesight. She continues to ask you for directions in a quivering voice.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Please follow me, ma'am. I'm heading in that direction anyway.
[Black Screen Wipe Transition]
After parting ways with Mrs. Jones, you return to your room with many things weighing on your mind. Just as you raise your hand to push the door open—
[Screen Flash + Circuit Breaker Sound Effect + Black Screen]
An ominous sound echoes throughout the train, followed by everything plunging into darkness. You blink and realize it's not that you've gone blind.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: A power outage...?

Now that you've been deprived of sight, your other senses sharpen in response. You hear the young train attendant shouting in the distance—something about water causing the aging electrical system to trip.
You're about to start finding your way through the darkness to grab a candle when you hear a scream from the other side of the door.

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: —Aaah?!
That's Clementine's voice! Has she been attacked?
[Black Screen]
Everything remains pitch black. You follow the sound, but you can only navigate by memory. You go through the suite's parlor and eventually into Clementine's bedroom.
As you fumble through the darkness, an arm suddenly wraps around you from behind, reaching past your neck to grip your shoulder. Instinct takes over. You seize the arm, drop your weight, and throw—

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Don't move!

The attacker tries to struggle, but you have them firmly pinned down with your weight. Yet, something feels wrong—the body under your hands is soft and slender, and that voice... it sounds strangely familiar...

steps.speaker: Familiar Voice
steps.content: Stop! Look closely... It's me!

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Clementine?
[Big CG - Close Contact A]
The curtains tear open amidst her struggling. Moonlight spills through the ripped fabric, illuminating you and Clementine.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Clementine? Where's the assailant? Did they get away—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh... umm... oopsies?
Clementine averts her gaze. You follow it and scan the room, only to find it completely empty. There's no sign of any attack.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That was just an act, huh? There was never anyone in here, was there? Did you do this on purpose?
[Big CG - Close Contact B]
Fabric brushes against your nose. Clementine cuts off your questioning with a smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Well, you took forever to get back. I was bored out of my mind.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The killer's been hiding on this train all day without making a move. My guess is they got cold feet and chickened out. So, I thought I'd liven things up and give them a little push!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A power outage, complete darkness... It's the perfect opportunity to strike. So tell me, why hasn't our killer made their move yet?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...That still doesn't justify scaring people on purpose.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: C'mon, don't be so upset. I'm perfectly fine, aren't I?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You came rushing in so quickly once you heard me scream... Were you worried about me? Weren't you afraid the attacker might still be in here?

options: ...Sounds like you were hoping for that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Looks to me that you were hoping they'd actually make their move during all that chaos.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're proving to be far more troublesome than that elusive killer we're after.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And you do realize that, if everyone in this carriage is a suspect, then that includes you too, right?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Pfft... Hahaha!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: My, looks like you caught me red-handed. You're absolutely right—my sworn enemy is on this train, trembling in fear at this very moment, terrified I might come knocking.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But an assassination in the dead of night? That's simply not my style. I prefer something grander, more spectacular—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Something like... setting everything ablaze and burning it all to the ground. How does that sound?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Huh?
[Background - Clementine's Compartment]
Crackle—the lights flicker back on with a soft buzz. The room is bright once more.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Wait, what did you mean by that?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Nothing. I just said that for fun.
"Don't take my jokes too seriously. Anyway, how's the investigation coming along? Did you find the other half of the letter?" your "employer" asks.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...I've made some progress. Not much, though.
[Darkened portraits appear as described in sequence: William → Mrs. Jones → Carl]

Your investigation so far has given you a basic understanding of the passengers on this train, but it's not enough for you to guess what they're thinking. Who is it that wrote that letter? And why would someone make such an insane threat?
Is it the thug with a long criminal record who suddenly showed up on this luxury train car?
Is it the elderly woman who inherited a fortune, yet seems so scatterbrained?
Or is it the young merchant whose words were so ambiguous, who seems to share some complicated history with Clementine?
Or perhaps, it's...
[Clementine's portrait appears, hold for 1 second]

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...It's late. The dining car has already closed, and the other passengers have likely locked their doors for the night. Any further investigation will have to wait until tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Perfect! We've been at this for hours. My shoulders are killing me...
Clementine stretches, then hands you the letter as she prepares to retreat to her room for the night. Before opening the door, she turns back and flashes you a smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Good night, detective.
You, too, tell her "goodnight" in return.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: See you tomorrow.
[Background - Clementine's Study, Extended 3-Second Transition]
You look up from the book and take a deep breath. Not much time has passed in reality—the tea beside you is still warm.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: So? Still tangled up with the "me" in the story?

options: Do you really need to ask?

steps.content: You raise your hand to rub your eyes, but you don't continue reading.
I give up. Let's just end this tedious charade already.
No internet, no Mania, only rudimentary electricity, on top of a train that's moving fast... It's certainly a compelling setting for a crime story.
You've definitely crafted a fascinating world different from DisCity, but what I'm looking for isn't some fiction, and certainly not the detective and Clementine playing some mystery-solving game.

options: Who's on the move in the real world?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hmm... Perhaps the information you seek is hidden in the first letter of each line? String them together, and you might just uncover some grand conspiracy!
You don't buy it. Clementine stands up with a smile and places the book before you once more.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Look, I know the plot's been too uneventful for your taste so far.
She turns another page for you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But I promise the good part is just around the corner...
